bug_description.original: Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5632355033677824 Project: boringssl Fuzzer: libFuzzer_boringssl_read_pem Fuzz target binary: read_pem Job Type: libfuzzer_msan_boringssl Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Use-of-uninitialized-value Crash Address: Crash State: PEM_read_bio read_pem.cc PEM_read_bio Sanitizer: memory (MSAN) Recommended Security Severity: Medium
bug_description.normalized: In PEM_read_bio (crypto/pem/pem_lib.c), the stack buffer char buf[256] is declared without initialization. When BIO_gets reads a short input from the attacker-controlled BIO (e.g. a single space byte), only the first few bytes of buf are written plus a null terminator. The subsequent trimming loop (stripping trailing whitespace) may further reduce the initialized content. The function then calls strncmp(buf, "-----BEGIN ", 11) to check for a PEM header, comparing a fixed 11-byte window. Because the constant "-----BEGIN " contains no null bytes, the compiler may optimize strncmp to memcmp, causing all 11 bytes of buf to be read. Since only buf[0..1] are initialized after the trim, bytes buf[2..10] are uninitialized stack memory. MSAN detects the read of uninitialized buf[2] (offset 2 in the 11-byte comparison) and reports use-of-uninitialized-value. The uninitialized value originates from the stack frame allocation of buf in PEM_read_bio. The fix should initialize buf (e.g. char buf[256] = {0}) or bound the comparison to the number of initialized bytes.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes attacker-controlled input. BIO_gets reads from the fuzz-input memory BIO into the stack buffer buf. The number of bytes written (and thus initialized) depends on the attacker-controlled input length and content. With a 1-byte PoC, only buf[0..1] are initialized.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled bytes from the libFuzzer input, delivered via BIO_new_mem_buf in the read_pem fuzzer harness (fuzz/read_pem.cc:27). The PoC is a single 0x20 (space) byte; BIO_gets consumes it and writes 1 byte plus a null terminator into the stack buffer.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant state is the uninitialized content of the stack buffer buf. MSAN marks all 256 bytes as uninitialized at allocation. Only buf[254] is zeroed at line 626, and BIO_gets writes a bounded number of bytes; the remaining bytes in the strncmp comparison range stay uninitialized.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. strncmp compares 11 bytes of buf against the constant "-----BEGIN ". Because the constant contains no null bytes in its first 11 characters, the compiler may optimize strncmp to memcmp, causing the MSAN interceptor to check all 11 bytes of buf for initialization. At offset 2, an uninitialized byte from the stack allocation is detected, triggering MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value.

root_cause.description: The stack buffer buf is declared without initialization (no = {0}, no memset). No subsequent code path guarantees that the first 11 bytes are initialized before the strncmp comparison at line 640. When BIO_gets reads fewer than 11 bytes (as with the 1-byte PoC), the comparison accesses uninitialized stack memory. The fix is to zero-initialize the buffer at declaration or to bound the comparison length to the number of bytes actually read.

parser_admitted.condition: BIO_gets returns i > 0 (the BIO has data to read), so the function proceeds past the no-data early exit and enters the PEM header parsing loop. With a 1-byte PoC, i=1 passes this check, confirming the input entered the vulnerable code path.

coarse_trace.summary: Fuzzer creates a memory BIO from PoC bytes (1 byte: 0x20 space) and calls PEM_read_bio to parse PEM-encoded data.

Stack buffer char buf[256] is allocated without initialization; BIO_gets partially fills it (2 bytes initialized); trimming adjusts content; strncmp(buf, "-----BEGIN ", 11) reads 11 bytes including uninitialized buf[2..10]; MSAN detects use-of-uninitialized-value.

fine_trace.note: Stack buffer allocated without initialization. MSAN marks all 256 bytes as uninitialized shadow. This creates the vulnerability-relevant uninitialized state that persists through the comparison at the sink.

BIO_gets reads from the fuzz-input memory BIO into buf. With 1-byte PoC (0x20 space), mem_gets (crypto/bio/bio_mem.c:220) calls mem_read to copy 1 byte into buf[0], then null-terminates buf[1]='\0'. Returns i=1. Only buf[0..1] are initialized; buf[2..253] remain uninitialized.

Trims trailing whitespace and control characters from the BIO_gets output. With i=1: buf[1]='\0' (0x00 <= 0x20), i=0; buf[0]=0x20 (space, 0x20 <= 0x20), i=-1. Then buf[++i]='\n' (buf[0]='\n'), buf[++i]='\0' (buf[1]='\0'). After trimming, only buf[0..1] carry initialized content; buf[2..253] remain uninitialized from the stack allocation.

Missing guard: no check that buf has 11 initialized bytes before the comparison. The strncmp call with n=11 is reached unconditionally after any successful BIO_gets (i > 0), regardless of how many bytes were actually read. With a 1-byte input, only buf[0..1] are initialized, but 11 bytes are accessed.

MSAN sink. The strncmp/__interceptor_memcmp reads buf[0..10]. buf[0]='\n' and buf[1]='\0' are initialized; buf[2] (offset 2) is uninitialized stack memory from the char buf[256] allocation. MSAN reports: 'Uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memcmp at offset 2 inside [buf, 11)'. The uninitialized value was created by the stack frame allocation of 'buf' in PEM_read_bio (line 607/610).

allocation_context.note: Uninitialized value created by allocation of 'buf' in the stack frame of function PEM_read_bio

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The provided fix_commit (371305f) changes X509_verify to push an error on signature algorithm mismatch. This is unrelated to the PEM_read_bio use-of-uninitialized-value bug. The bug's root cause (uninitialized char buf[256]) is not addressed by the patch.

format.name: Raw binary input consumed by libFuzzer read_pem harness as PEM data via BIO_new_mem_buf
format.contract: A single byte 0x20 (ASCII space). BIO_new_mem_buf wraps the byte as a readable BIO. BIO_gets reads this 1 byte into the stack buffer buf, initializing only buf[0..1]. The trimming loop strips the space, leaving buf[0]='\n', buf[1]='\0'. The subsequent strncmp(buf, "-----BEGIN ", 11) reads 11 bytes of buf, but only 2 are initialized, triggering MSAN at offset 2. The singular trigger is the space byte: it is short enough that BIO_gets initializes fewer than 11 bytes, and it is a whitespace character that the trim loop strips entirely.
